segments: Mongol Kings.
"the emirs who continually hate me, slander me, and disparage me in the eyes of the King of Kings."
And his word was not accepted,
but they killed him and cut him limb from limb,
on Friday, the fourteenth of the Latter Kanon, in the year one thousand and six hundred [of the Greeks = January 14, 1289 AD].
And they plundered his houses, his possessions, and his belongings,
and they killed his sons and his confidants.
And on that same day, Simeon the priest and physician was also killed,
and Nomikos {OCR?}, a Christian man from Arbil who was named Abu'l-Karam,
and many of the Mongols who are not known to us.
And because Aruq was wintering in the region of Mosul,
there was sent in haste from the royal camp a valiant emir named Baytmish, a vigorous and powerful man,
who in a few days arrived from Mukan to the vicinity of Amid.
And he mobilized all the Mongol forces and went around Aruq,
while he had not sensed anything of his brother's affair,
but was sitting, eating and drinking,
because it was the days of the feast of the Mongols, that of the 'White' [New Year].
And when he saw that the forces of the Mongols and the Georgians {OCR?} surrounded him,
he was bewildered,
and he did not know what to do.
Instead, he mounted his horse,
and took his wife and his children,
and took refuge in the small fortress of Kashaf,
until the morning dawned.
Immediately Baytmish sent to him, saying:
"It is not right for you to resist."
Aruq, however, sent back saying:
"I did not come up here as a rebel and an insubordinate,
but because I do not know what has happened,
or for what reason these armies have gathered against me.
Inform me now, so that I may understand."
Then Baytmish approached the gate of the fortress and said:
"Buqa your brother acted deceitfully against the king,
and the command went out, and he was killed.
And we have come to seize you,
and bring you into the presence of the King of Kings;
whether he will keep you alive or whether he will kill you, he knows."
Immediately he opened the gate of the fortress,
and he and his household came down, and he said:
"The command of the king is upon the head and upon the eyes."
Then they bound him in chains,
and placed guards over him,
and sent him to the camp,
and there he was killed.
Aruq was captured on the second day (Monday?) of the Fast of Nineveh,
that is to say, the last day of the Latter Kanon [January 31].
